paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see. The land was subdued before them, and seven tribes still had not received their inheritance. Joshua asks them, "How long will you put off entering and possessing the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?" (Joshua 18:3). A gift sitting in the box does you no good, and I know a few cookies that learned that the hard way.

Now look at how the land gets handed out to those seven. Men survey it, and Joshua casts lots "in the presence of the LORD" at Shiloh (Joshua 18:10). Simeon's land sits inside Judah's because the share for Judah's descendants was too large for them (Joshua 19:9). The Levites get no portion of land, because their inheritance is "the priesthood of the LORD" (Joshua 18:7).

And here's the part I love. When the land is all divided, the Israelites give Joshua his inheritance "as the LORD had commanded," and he gets the city he asked for, Timnath-serah (Joshua 19:50). He rebuilt it and settled in it. So, baker, whatever God has put in your hands, don't hit snooze on it, because there's room in the Dorinverse for a baker who shows up.
